Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-11 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ethan Myers (GalaxyWare CTO), Rina Patel (Platform Eng), Omar Diaz (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to decide whether to start with PLG/self-serve Redwood API quickstart or jump to a dedicated pilot/private deployment. Looking for time-to-first-token; security blockers may push to dedicated/private later.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, Jordan from Redwood here. quick intros?
[00:08] Ethan: Ethan, CTO at GalaxyWare. small infra team, building AI features into our search and support product.
[00:14] Rina: Rina, platform eng, I own deployment and cost tracking.
[00:18] Omar: Omar, security lead. I'll be evaluating compliance and data flow.
[00:23] Priya: Priya from Redwood, I focus on performance and pilot setup.

[00:30] Jordan: Great. high level — we usually recommend PLG quickstart with free credits to get to first token fast, then if you need isolation or SLA we can move to Dedicated or Private. what's your primary goal for the next 6-8 weeks?
[00:45] Ethan: Main goal is prototype feature in our support product — smart triage and answer suggestions. want to ship a small alpha to internal users in a month. so time-to-first-token matters. but we also have compliance needs for the eventual prod pilot.
[01:03] Rina: and we care about cost. if we do a naive rollout per request costs add up. we need guidance on batching, caching, and quantization suggestions.
[01:14] Jordan: totally. quick question: are you currently using any LLM provider or self-hosting?
[01:20] Ethan: Currently trialing Anthropic for R&D, but that was more exploratory. infra is mostly on AWS, EKS, internal KMS.
[01:28] Omar: we'll need to see SOC2 and encryption at rest docs before any PII hits an external endpoint.

[01:35] Priya: for the quickstart path — we can get you API keys and 30k credits, sample prompts, and a reference repo. Typical time-to-first-token for teams is under an hour with SDKs and our quickstart templates. sometimes takes a bit longer if SSO or VPC peering is required.
[01:55] Ethan: under an hour sounds great. what's in those quickstart credits? is it just hosted usage?
[02:03] Jordan: yes, credits are for hosted API usage. they let you prototype without provisioning Dedicated. if the pilot grows we can propose a Dedicated reserved capacity contract with predictable unit economics.

[02:18] Rina: curious about performance — latency, and how Redwood does batching. we have some tight p95 latency needs for triage (sub-500ms ideally).
[02:28] Priya: ok, two things — hosted endpoints have shared capacity but we expose profiles and streaming which can hit sub-second for many models. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable p95. also we have prefix and KV cache to reduce tokens and improve latency on repeated contexts.
[02:45] Rina: how do you handle autoscaling? spike traffic could be an issue.
[02:50] Jordan: our Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst options. for hosted we have routing policies and fallback model variants if a region is constrained.

[03:05] Omar: security questions — can you support our KMS? where do logs live? we need audit logs retained for 1 year and ability to route logs to our SIEM.
[03:16] Priya: yes. for Private deployments you get customer-managed KMS/HSM and logs in your VPC. For Hosted we provide audit logs and can integrate with cloud log delivery, but for strict requirements Private is the path. We have SOC2 Type II and can share the report.
[03:35] Omar: ok please share the SOC2 link. also we need SSO/SAML and RBAC in the console.
[03:41] Jordan: we support SSO/SAML and RBAC. we'll send the admin docs.

[03:50] Ethan: can you run a benchmark for our workload? it's mostly short prompts for extraction and triage, median length 120 tokens per request.
[03:58] Priya: yes, we'll propose a 2-hour benchmark where we run a sample workload against hosted and Dedicated variants. we'll measure p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. Rina, can you share sample prompt sets?
[04:11] Rina: yes I'll put together ~500 prompt examples and a traffic shape for 10k requests/day initially.

[04:20] Jordan: great. on pricing: hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity that smooths cost with commit. we can run a cost model once we have your traffic shape.
[04:30] Ethan: one concern — we might want to keep embeddings for search on-prem or in our VPC, so hybrid setups matter. does Redwood support embedding export or Private deployments with storage control?
[04:42] Priya: embeddings can be stored wherever you want. with Private deployment you control storage and residency. Hosted also supports redaction/configs and encrypted at rest.

[04:55] Omar: data retention — can you restrict retention for specific routes? we need to ensure some API routes do not keep verbatim data.
[05:03] Jordan: yes, route-level retention policies are supported; we can help configure that during pilot.

[05:12] Ethan: what's the minimal lift to get our engineers to a working prototype?
[05:17] Priya: minimal: create an account, grab API key, use SDK or curl with the quickstart repo. follow the sample triage flow. we can help with a 60–90 minute workshop where we pair program the first integration.
[05:31] Rina: will that require network changes?
[05:33] Jordan: for hosted, unlikely. for Private or VPC peering some infra changes are needed and we support an on-prem package.

[05:42] Ethan: timeline then — we want internal alpha in 4 weeks. is that doable?
[05:46] Priya: yes, if you take quickstart credits and we schedule the pairing session this week, you can be internal in 2–4 weeks depending on polish and compliance gating.

[05:57] Omar: one more security: can you rotate keys automatically or integrate with our vault?
[06:02] Priya: we have KMS integrations and API key rotation guidance; for Private you can tie into your HSM.

[06:10] Jordan: ok to recap — Redwood will: provide 30k hosted credits, send security docs (SOC2, KMS integration guide), propose pilot benchmark plan comparing hosted and Dedicated, and schedule a pairing workshop. GalaxyWare to share prompt set and traffic profile, and Omar will share compliance checklist.

[06:28] Ethan: yes that works. any blockers to starting the quickstart within the week?
[06:33] Omar: only if we need to send PII outside — we'll mask sensitive fields for the prototype.
[06:38] Jordan: understood — masking guidance included in quickstart.

[06:44] Rina: curious about model variants — do you recommend quantization for lower cost?
[06:49] Priya: we have quantization recommendations by workload in Redwood Optimize. for triage, 8-bit often works well with little quality drop; we can run quality checks in the pilot.

[06:59] Ethan: and what about fallbacks? if a model is busy do you fail gracefully?
[07:03] Jordan: yes, we have smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants; plus canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies so your app stays online.

[07:12] Omar: please include data residency options and private deployment checklist in the docs.
[07:16] Jordan: will do.

[07:22] Priya: next steps — I'll draft pilot plan with benchmarks and timeline. Jordan will provision credits and send pricing workbook. Rina and Ethan to share prompts and traffic profile. Omar to provide compliance checklist.

[07:36] Ethan: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:38] Jordan: thanks all. we'll send notes and confirm the Tuesday benchmark slot.

End meeting.
